CS5-01.note: The colon glosses the blank outright ('a residue of manufacture with no bearing on how the sheet aged'), so the reversal that follows is not even needed. B is what the surveys show, not what curators assumed; D is the opposite of the buffering finding. Correct but under-loaded for module 2.

CS5-02.note: 'males recorded forty years apart shared the same terminal trill' fixes the blank before the reversal arrives. The vocabulary tier (stochastic/attenuated/polymorphic) is the only load, and 'invariant' is the common word of the four.

CS5-03.note: Both B (flakes badly) and D (copied wholesale from maiolica) are asserted in the passage, which makes them genuinely attractive; only A is what the isotope finding refutes, since the isotopes make the glaze assignable to a kiln without touching either its fragility or its derivativeness. The best-built completion item in the set.

CS5-04.note: Requires reading 'one hand working once and at leisure' as after the fact, then seeing that eleven ink changes at port calls and later days written into earlier days' margins prove serial composition. B is the trap for anyone who maps the evidence to the blank instead of to its refutation, and the closing sentence explicitly disarms A.

CS5-05.note: 'neither is the quicker to work with: the same synchronisms must be checked either way' is an explicit block on B, and the last sentence names parsimony in so many words ('adds fewer unattested entities'). C is off-register for a chronology argument, D only loosely live. Works as written.

CS5-06.note: I read 'register' as give outward sign: the evidence is about MANNER (same hand, same clipped syntax as the price of oats), not omission, so the account shows no sign of the loss. But B is live on the text as written - the diary records the flood's facts and never names the loss as a loss, i.e. never acknowledges it - and nothing in the passage separates the two. C is correctly killed by the chair sentence. This item was not on the author's list and should be.

CS5-07.note: A is blocked ('satisfied nobody', 'nothing in the mechanics justified'). But once 'clarified' is gone, B and D are both supported by exactly the same sentences: a mean adopted for no mechanical reason, purely so the search could proceed, is a question quieted as much as concluded. And B is the default sense of 'settled' applied to a question, so it is also the blind guess.

CS5-08.note: 'It is not spare' is an explicit block on A, and the whole middle of the passage is about substituting phrases a farmer could act on. B would need candour, which is nowhere in the text; D is refuted by 'a choice rather than a limitation'.

CS5-09.note: Flat boulders hold snow six weeks longer, so less growing season, so thalli smaller than age alone implies - which is exactly the third-smaller observation the curve read as youth. The four options are a clean 2x2 over {surface} x {direction}, so nothing is gettable by shape and a sign error costs the item. Best function item in the set.

CS5-10.note: The evidence the second sentence is tested against is the fee (three times a week's wage, paid regardless) and the unissued masters. B is a good trap because both of its nouns appear in the text, but the denied royalty is part of sentence one's setup, not the test. A and C name evidence the text never supplies.

CS5-11.note: The last sentence reconciles 80% survival with flat canopy by saying the survivors stay small and never close. B asserts an equality the text does not state; D invents a measurement threshold; A contradicts 'a decade of work along the delta'.

CS5-12.note: Two reasons, both undercutting: the narrow terms already existed on the guild rolls, and the 1806 form revision changed what clerks were prompted to write. D inverts the second reason (the clerks' form changed, not their competence), which is the one real trap.

CS5-13.note: All four options share the first two clauses, so only the tail is in play, and the closing sentence is plainly about added biomass and per-cut funding. A misreads the ending's valence, D invents a dispute. Straightforward.

CS5-14.note: 'which suggests storage rather than flight' hands over the tail. B is beaten by that same clause and C is contradicted twice over. Valid, but there is nothing left to do after the last six words.

CS5-15.note: 'only by a fifth of the gap' and 'the remainder tracks the concentration of a small solute' are lifted straight into C. The other three are numeric mismatches, so this is a matching exercise rather than a structure judgement.

CS5-16.note: Key is stated almost verbatim ('asked to say where a psalm turns, agree with one another far less often'). A is eliminable WITHOUT the passage: B, C and D all read 'help readers ...' and A alone reads 'cost the psalm ...', so the frame break isolates it and a blind solver is at 1 in 3. Worse than the author's description.

CS5-17.note: A is a well-set trap: the overnight agreement is in the passage but functions as the control that rules out sensor error, not as the comparison the text exists to report. B and C name comparisons never made.

CS5-18.note: 'the lyre, and no other instrument, accompanies the walk to the church' plus 'the instrument they came home to play was the one the rite required' states A directly. C is killed by the isolation paragraph and D by the fiddlers who did travel and came back.

CS5-19.note: Every piece of evidence in Text 2 is about the doors: order of refurbishment, biggest gain where the corridor was brightest, no gain where the doors were already done. The actigraphy inversion HOLDS - A is the fact a well-read solver reaches for, but Text 2 only names the instrument and never criticises it, so A is not defensible on the text as written. One cost: the actigraphy clause does no work except as bait.

CS5-20.note: The legume inversion HOLDS: A is the field's stock answer and is explicitly neutralised ('every plot is fertilized to the same soil-nitrogen target'), as is C by 'weed counts are the same in both systems'. B is what 'What differs is the calendar' introduces. D is unanchored - nobody scores soil structure in either text - but it is not blind-eliminable.

CS5-21.note: Text 2's whole first sentence is the counting change, and the household surveys confirm it. B, C and D each require a fact neither text supplies. Clean but thin.

CS5-22.note: Text 2 disputes the CAUSE and concedes the effect ('Submission counts fall wherever the odds ... are visibly worse'), so the shared claim is the submission shortfall. C is the standard one-author trap - true of Text 2 only. Agreement items are structurally easy and this one is no exception.

CS5-23.note: Two outcomes crossed with two verdicts, and the last sentence splits them: matched time equalises recall (so rehearsal does not explain the recall gap) but not reproduction (so it does). A and D are both single-clause misreadings of the same sentence, and D is the attractive over-correction.

CS5-24.note: June-before versus late-August-after, with most shoot growth in July, is a measurement artefact, and the same-month reaches showing no change settles it. The water-table inversion HOLDS - A is the stock hydrological answer and is shut off by a flat denial - as is B by 'reaches with ponds gained no more height'. D is unanchored filler.

CS5-05.verdict: Not broken. The senses do cluster, but the passage disarms them one at a time: 'neither is the quicker to work with' is an explicit block on Efficiency, Prosperity is off-register for a chronology dispute, and the closing sentence defines Parsimony without naming it. The cost is difficulty, not validity - it grades medium because the block is explicit rather than inferred.

CS5-07.verdict: Two problems, not one. The author named the blind default: 'Concluded' is both the key and the highest-prior sense of 'settled' applied to a question, so this item will score above chance in a no-source attack. The second problem is with source - D 'Quieted' is defensible on the text as written. A question closed by an unjustified average that satisfied nobody, adopted only so the search could proceed, is quieted at least as well as concluded, and no sentence separates the two. Either block D the way A is blocked ('clarified' is killed outright), or key a non-default sense.

CS5-14.verdict: C is dead on contact with 'The western hoards do not cluster at all', but it is not eliminable blind, so it costs difficulty rather than validity. The real weakness is elsewhere: 'which suggests storage rather than flight' hands over the answer tail in six words, which is why this grades easy.

CS5-16.verdict: The author described A as rejectable. It is rejectable WITHOUT READING ANYTHING. B, C and D all open 'To explain why the older rendering's inversions help readers ...'; A alone reads 'cost the psalm its English idiom'. The odd-man-out is visible in the option set alone, so a blind solver is at 1 in 3 before the passage opens - this is the axis-alignment failure mode, an option differing along the axis the stem names. Recast A inside the same frame (something of the form 'help readers hear the Hebrew word order at the cost of English idiom') so the frame stops marking it. This is the one item in the batch I would hold.

CS5-20.verdict: D is unanchored - neither text scores soil structure by any method - but it is not blind-eliminable and the key is decided by explicit calendar evidence, so the item works. The legume inversion the repair was aiming for does hold: A is the field's stock answer and is shut off by the same-nitrogen-target clause.

not_flagged_by_author_but_should_be.CS5-06: Live second reading. I key D (give outward sign) on the manner evidence - same hand, same clipped syntax as the price of oats - but B (acknowledge) survives the passage as written, since the diary records the flood's particulars and never names the loss as a loss. Nothing in the text discriminates. Add a clause that makes the diary's silence a matter of showing rather than of mentioning, or drop one of the two options.
not_flagged_by_author_but_should_be.CS5-19: Not broken, but the actigraphy clause in Text 2 does no argumentative work at all; its only function is to bait option A. That is legitimate SAT practice, noted only so nobody later 'tidies' it into a criticism of actigraphy, which would make A defensible and break the item.

by_question_stem.template: blank completion, 'most logical and precise word or phrase'
words in context, 'As used in the text ... most nearly mean'

by_question_stem.note: Six paired-text items, but the stems inside it vary (three 'how would Text 2 respond', one agreement, one 'role of', one 'what the evidence implies'), and the domain blueprint expects cross-text connections. Not a defect, but it is the largest single template in the batch.

by_option_shape.template: shared-prefix option frame: all four options repeat an identical long stem and vary only in the tail clause
by_option_shape.note: This is the batch's real cross-item template and it is the LEAK-SUPPRESSING one - holding all four options in a single frame is what keeps the option set from deciding the item without the source. Two consequences worth recording rather than fixing blindly. (1) Uniformity: 15 of 24 items look identical in outline, so a student who learns the tail-comparison habit applies one procedure to most of the batch, which is part of why so many grade easy. (2) It is only safe while every tail stays inside the frame - CS5-16 is the item where the frame broke, and that break is precisely the defect found there.

by_option_shape.template: explicit-blocker construction: a clause in the passage kills the most attractive distractor outright
by_option_shape.note: Five items are decided by a single flat denial ('neither is the quicker to work with', 'It is not spare', 'fertilized to the same soil-nitrogen target', 'The water table did not move'). This is what makes the stock-answer inversions work, and it is also a repeatable tell: find the sentence that denies something and the distractor it denies is the trap. A solver who notices the pattern gets a reliable shortcut across those five.
